atoms.b: Some differences can be more meaningful than others. They can play a ((++larger smaller)) role in our interactions with other people and lead to ((++conflict love)) if not handled properly.

trainers.hint: A meaningful difference is one that can change how people are treated, included or understood.

atoms.a: being a boy or a girl

feedback.wrong: While being a boy or a girl is not better than the other, it is a very important factor in our lives that will affect our interactions with one another.
People with disabilities face certain struggles that people who are not disabled don’t. People who are not in wheelchairs do not have to think about ensuring they are able to get around.
People who grow up with more money are often given opportunities that people with less money don’t get. This can have a big impact on someone’s experiences and future.

atoms.a: living next to a forest or a river

feedback.wrong: While these environments can be pretty different, we generally don’t think of this difference as being very important.
Different cultures have different customs and traditions. These differences require careful consideration and understanding.

atoms.a: being from a family of musicians or from a family of painters

feedback.wrong: Although these jobs are different from each other, it is not a difference that will easily lead to conflict or misunderstandings.

instruction.text: Read the text and decide who has the more meaningful difference.

atoms.a: James is planning on cooking some roast pork. His friend, Devi, is a Muslim. According to her religion, she cannot eat pork. Another friend, Michael, also doesn’t eat pork because he doesn’t like the taste of it.
atoms.sound: James is planning on cooking some roast pork. His friend, Devvi, is a Muslim. According to her religion, she cannot eat pork. Another friend, Michael, also doesn’t eat pork because he doesn’t like the taste of it.

feedback.end: A religious difference is more serious than a difference related to a like or dislike.

atoms.a: Amy wants to go to a party. She asks her friends if they would like to join. However, Margaret has had a long day and wants to rest, and Hong has terrible social anxiety and hates parties.

feedback.end: While both reasons for not wanting to go to the party should be respected, feeling tired is different from social anxiety. If Margaret wasn’t tired, perhaps she would want to go, whereas Hong’s anxiety is likely to be a more constant feeling.

atoms.a: Megan doesn’t really like dogs and tries to avoid them. However, her friends, Adam and Jake, like dogs. Adam mostly just pets the dogs he comes across, but Jake really loves dogs and owns a lot of them.

feedback.end: It is often important just how much someone likes a certain thing. If one person doesn’t like it while the other really loves it, this makes the difference more meaningful.
